question_text: A 42-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after having a seizure. His wife states that the patient has been struggling with alcohol abuse and has recently decided to "quit once and for all". Physical exam is notable for a malnourished patient responsive to verbal stimuli. He has moderate extremity weakness, occasional palpitations, and brisk deep tendon reflexes (DTRs). EKG demonstrates normal sinus rhythm and a prolonged QT interval. What nutritional deficiency most likely contributed to these findings?
